title: BitcoinNetworkSimulator scenario
description: A scenario file is a mapping with a top-level Phases list (applied in order: phase 0's settings and NodeGroups take effect immediately, and each later phase's settings/NodeGroups take over once the previous phase's DurationSeconds elapses — a field a phase leaves out inherits whatever the previous phase had in effect, or the built-in default for phase 0) and an optional top-level NodeRules list (named ConsensusRules a NodeGroup can point to by name via RulesName, instead of every group that shares one repeating the same block). See Scenario.cs and the "Scenarios" section of README.md for the authoritative reference.

NodeRules.description: A named library of ConsensusRules a NodeGroup can reference by RulesName instead of repeating the same block inline. Two entries sharing a Name is a scenario-authoring mistake (the last one silently wins) — keep names unique.

DefaultRuleSchedule.description: Controls which RuleSchedule organically-grown nodes follow (organic growth / AutoGrowth-created nodes, and the initial dynamic-start node — never NodeGroups-authored nodes, which always use their own RulesName/RuleSchedule). Each entry is a TRANCHE, active for nodes created at or after its FromHeight: its RuleSchedules array is the full distribution new nodes are drawn from for that stage of the network's growth. A later tranche replaces an earlier one outright once the network reaches it, rather than blending with it. See the ScenarioDefaultRuleScheduleEntry doc comment in Scenario.cs for the full worked examples.

Description.description: Purely informational — echoed to the console when this phase becomes active, so a scenario file is self-explanatory without needing a separate README to cross-reference.

DurationSeconds.description: How long this phase lasts before the next one in the list takes over, exactly as if Enter had been pressed and the run restarted with the next phase's settings. For the *last* phase, this instead means how long the whole run lasts before automatically shutting down. Omitted on the last phase means no automatic stop — waits indefinitely for Enter. Omitted on any earlier phase means that phase never ends on its own — later phases never activate — so every non-last phase should set this.

AutoGrowth.description: Whether the network keeps growing organically on top of whatever NodeGroups create. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (true for phase 0, matching behavior with no scenario at all); set false to freeze the network at its current node count for this phase's duration.

GrowthIntervalSeconds.description: How often organic growth ticks. Only consulted when AutoGrowth is true. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (NodeNetwork.DefaultGrowthIntervalMs for phase 0).

GrowthRate.description: Multiplier applied to the current node count each growth tick. 2.0 (the default) doubles the network every tick; 1.5 adds 50% more nodes per tick. A value at or below 1.0 stalls growth entirely — the tick keeps firing but never adds a node. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (2.0 for phase 0).

GrowthJitterSeconds.description: Random +/- range applied to GrowthIntervalSeconds on every tick, so growth doesn't land on a perfectly metronomic schedule. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (0 for phase 0 — no jitter).

GrowthMinSeedNodes.description: Floor the network tops up to — one node per tick, ignoring GrowthRate — before exponential growth-rate scaling takes over. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (0 for phase 0 — no floor). Useful when this phase's NodeGroups (or the single-node default start) seed fewer nodes than you want established before the network starts compounding.

MaxNodes.description: Hard cap organic growth will not exceed. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (NodeNetwork.DefaultMaxNodes for phase 0).

OutboundPeerCount.description: How many outbound peers each node picks at creation — see the "Peer topology" note in README.md. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (8 for phase 0, matching real Bitcoin).

GrowthMaliciousFraction.description: Fraction of newly-created nodes (both the initial dynamic-start node and every node organic growth adds during this phase) assigned a malicious role instead of Honest, cycling through the four malicious types in order. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (0.5 for phase 0). Only affects nodes with no metadata.json yet; NodeGroups-authored nodes always use their own Role.

GrowthWalletOnlyFraction.description: Fraction of newly-created nodes assigned wallet-only (CanMine false) instead of mining-capable. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (1/3 for phase 0). Same "no metadata.json yet" scope as GrowthMaliciousFraction.

ChurnIntervalSeconds.description: How often node churn ticks — see ChurnRate. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (NodeNetwork.DefaultChurnIntervalMs for phase 0).

ChurnRate.description: Fraction of the current node count removed each churn tick (floored — a low rate on a small network simply skips removal that tick rather than over-shrinking it). Nodes leaving the live network is the counterpart to organic growth, and runs whenever this is above 0, independent of AutoGrowth. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (0 for phase 0 — disabled, nodes never leave).

ChurnMinNodes.description: Floor churn will never shrink the network below. Omitted inherits the previous phase's value (1 for phase 0 — mining needs at least one node to make progress).

NodeGroups.description: Each entry describes Count identically-configured nodes to add when this phase begins, applied in the order listed and added on top of whatever nodes already exist from earlier phases — e.g. a later phase modeling "mining pools emerge" might add a Pool-tagged group without touching anything already running. An empty/omitted list means "no explicit nodes this phase"; for phase 0 specifically, an empty/omitted list also means Program falls back to its normal single-node default start.

Count.description: How many identically-configured nodes this group creates.

Role.description: Honest nodes behave correctly. The four malicious roles are deliberately misbehaving, each caught a different way: Equivocator forces real forks/reorgs, Impersonator is rejected by BuiltBy signature verification, Corruptor is rejected by hash/PoW re-checks, and Withholder's partial gossip gets caught up via full-chain broadcast.

HashPower.description: Simulated hash power — higher values win proportionally more mining rounds, not deterministically every time.

CostPerAttempt.description: $ cost of a single mining attempt (one nonce tried) — see "Mining costs" in README.md. Only consulted for a ValueSeeking group: if the best candidate's value doesn't clear CostPerAttempt x HashPower this turn, the group sits idle instead of mining at a guaranteed loss. Default 0 means mining is free (unchanged behavior).

CostOfLiving.description: $ fixed cost this group's node owes every turn, REGARDLESS of whether it mines — unlike CostPerAttempt, which is only owed while attempting nonces. See "Cost of living" in README.md. Only meaningful for a ValueSeeking group. If accrued cost ever exceeds this node's on-chain net worth plus StartingCapital, it is forced out of the network (churned) — real hash power going bankrupt. Default 0 means no living cost (unchanged behavior).

StartingCapital.description: $ runway this group's node starts with, on top of its on-chain balance's market value, before CostOfLiving can push it into insolvency. Without this, a brand-new node with CostOfLiving set would go bankrupt on its very first turn.

CanMine.description: Whether this group ever gets a mining turn. A node with CanMine false still fully validates, gossips, and sends/receives transactions — it just never builds a block itself (wallet-only).

Pool.description: Null/omitted mines solo (default). Otherwise, the name of a mining pool this group subscribes to — its HashPower is combined with every other current member's into the pool's single shared turn instead of getting its own. Only honored for Role Honest; a malicious role's Pool value, if set, is ignored and it always mines solo.

EconomicWeight.description: How heavily this group is weighted when other nodes are choosing their outbound peers — see the "Peer topology" note in README.md. 1 is an ordinary node; higher values make this group's nodes proportionally more likely to be picked as another node's outbound peer, turning them into structural hubs.

RulesName.description: Shorthand for a single-entry RuleSchedule ({ FromHeight: 0, RulesName }) — this group's ConsensusRules for its whole life, by name from the scenario file's top-level NodeRules list. Every node validates INCOMING blocks against its OWN currently-active rules for that height, not whatever a block itself claims (see Blockchain.cs's RuleSchedule) — so another group (or scenario) whose schedule agrees at a given height stays in consensus with this one, and one that disagrees diverges (a simulated fork), same as real Bitcoin vs. an incompatible fork client. Omitted (or a name not defined in NodeRules) means every ConsensusRules field defaults. Ignored (with a warning) if RuleSchedule is also set.

RuleSchedule.description: This group's full timeline of which named ruleset is active at which block height — e.g. real-bitcoin from height 0, switching to a different named ruleset from height 6 on. Takes precedence over RulesName if both are set.

ValueSeeking.description: Whether this group dynamically picks its ruleset each height by live profitability (NominalBlockReward x PriceSchedule) instead of a fixed RulesName/RuleSchedule — see "ValueSeeking" in README.md. Takes precedence over RulesName/RuleSchedule if both are set and ValueSeekingCandidates resolves to at least one valid entry.

ValueSeekingCandidates.description: Names of NodeRules entries this group compares when ValueSeeking is true. A name not defined in NodeRules is a scenario-authoring mistake (logged as a warning, skipped).

FromHeight.description: The named ruleset below becomes active starting at this block height (inclusive), until a later entry (if any) supersedes it. Include a FromHeight: 0 entry to cover genesis onward — an empty gap before the first entry's FromHeight resolves to ConsensusRules' own defaults.

RulesName.description: Name of an entry in the scenario file's top-level NodeRules list, active from FromHeight on. Referencing a name not defined in NodeRules is a scenario-authoring mistake (logged as a warning; falls back to defaults for this entry).

FromHeight.description: This tranche only applies to nodes created once the network's chain has reached this block height (inclusive), replacing whichever earlier tranche was active outright. Omitted defaults to 0 — applies from the very first organically-created node on.

RuleSchedules.description: The full distribution new nodes created under this tranche are drawn from — an array of weighted options (Percents summed in list order against a 100-point pool; whatever's left unclaimed falls back to a node's hardcoded ConsensusRules defaults).

Percent.description: What percentage (0-100, not a 0-1 fraction) of new nodes created under this tranche should be assigned RulesName, decided by random chance per node.

RulesName.description: Name of an entry in the scenario file's top-level NodeRules list, assigned as the Percent share's single, lifelong ConsensusRules. Referencing a name not defined in NodeRules is a scenario-authoring mistake (logged as a warning; falls back to defaults).

FromHeight.description: Price below becomes this ruleset's $-reference value starting at this block height (inclusive), until a later entry (if any) supersedes it.

Price.description: This ruleset's $ value from FromHeight on. Only consulted by a ValueSeeking NodeGroup's profitability comparison (NominalBlockReward x Price).

Name.description: How a ScenarioNodeGroup.RulesName refers to this entry. Keep unique within NodeRules — a duplicate Name is a scenario-authoring mistake (the last one silently wins).

RetargetIntervalBlocks.description: How often (in blocks) proof-of-work difficulty retargets. Defaults to real Bitcoin's own 2016-block window.

TargetSecondsPerBlock.description: How long a block "should" take on average; retargeting pushes difficulty toward this pace. Defaults to real Bitcoin's own 10-minute (600s) target.

MinAdjustmentFactor.description: Floor on how much easier a single retarget can make the target (0.25 = at most 4x easier). Already real Bitcoin's own clamp.

MaxAdjustmentFactor.description: Ceiling on how much harder a single retarget can make the target (4 = at most 4x harder). Already real Bitcoin's own clamp.

InitialDifficultyShift.description: Higher = harder (lower per-attempt mining success probability). Deliberately NOT matched to real Bitcoin's actual difficulty, which would make a block practically unmineable here — mining only gets a bounded number of attempts per turn (this group's HashPower), not the unbounded, massively-parallel search a real miner performs.

InitialBlockReward.description: Coinbase reward for the very first block, before any halving. Defaults to real Bitcoin's own 50 coins.

HalvingIntervalBlocks.description: How often (in blocks) the coinbase reward halves. Defaults to real Bitcoin's own 210,000-block interval.

MaxSupply.description: Hard cap on total coins ever minted across the whole chain. Defaults to real Bitcoin's own 21,000,000 — which the default InitialBlockReward/HalvingIntervalBlocks pair converges to asymptotically, so the cap actually binds. Overriding InitialBlockReward/HalvingIntervalBlocks for a faster-paced run without also scaling this down means the cap may no longer bind in practice.

PriceSchedule.description: This ruleset's $-reference value over height — see "ValueSeeking" in README.md. Omitted means worth $0 at every height (never picked over any priced alternative by a value-seeking node).
